reference.context: Canonical reference for outstanding chores for the project. Chores are small actionable items that need to be addressed, but do not take priority over active development work.

chore.synopsis: Define canonical serialization for ExtractionTrace (recommendation: model_dump_json/model_validate_json round-trip with custom INCOMPLETE serializer/validator pair); choose persistence shape (sibling JSON vs embedded vs separate store).

chores.chore: v3.0 ships `ExtractionTrace` with in-memory-identity-only semantics for the `INCOMPLETE` sentinel — `model_dump_json()` round-trips will not preserve the sentinel because no custom serializer/validator pair is wired. This is intentional per spec §6.2: persistence questions belong to the consumer-layer (CLI/GUI) session that introduces a storage transport, not to the in-memory contract that this plan establishes. Method per spec §2 in-flight chore: when a consumer session lands trace persistence, define the canonical serialization shape. Recommendation (informational only; commitment lives in the consumer's session): adopt `model_dump_json()` / `model_validate_json()` as the canonical round-trip and ship a custom serializer/validator pair for `INCOMPLETE` (e.g., serialized as a tagged string and validated back to the sentinel via identity replacement). The same exercise resolves whether the trace persists alongside the trust as a sibling JSON, embedded in TrustData metadata, or in a separate store. Exit criteria: a brief design note documenting the chosen persistence shape, ratified by the consumer session that introduces it. Blast radius: design note plus the consumer session's storage layer plus a small `trace.py` patch wiring the custom INCOMPLETE serializer. Gated by a consumer-layer session for trust persistence existing — no plan currently scheduled, so this chore stays open until that work surfaces. Cross-references plans index 5 (shared-firm-config / SharePoint) as a candidate co-located transport.

chore.synopsis: Calibrate AnthropicBackend token-usage CI ceiling from N≥3 cycle-15 observations; pin a noise-tolerant percentile assertion in test_anthropic_backend_integration.py once enough observations have accumulated in Green commit messages.

chores.chore: Plan-group #14 (instrumentation) cycle 15 ships observation-only: each live call's `response.usage` block is captured via test-side monkey-patch on `backend._client.messages.create`, printed to stdout, and recorded in the Green commit message. No in-test ceiling assertion lands in Plan A. Rationale (per plan-review I1): with extended thinking enabled (spec §8.3) and only N=1 observation available at execution time, a pinned ceiling of 1.5× one warm-cache observation is noise-bait — token counts vary substantially on identical prompts and CI would flake. Spec §9.2's "calibrated at execution time" is satisfied by recording, not by asserting. Surface-ready when: ≥3 observations per mechanism (`output_config` and `tool_use`) accumulate across separate opt-in cycle-15 runs. The credit-cap gate (auto-memory project-anthropic-api-credit-cap; ANTHROPIC_SMOKE_CONFIRM_SPEND=y) means observations accrue slowly — likely ~3 weeks of normal opt-in smoke usage. The chore stays open until observations exist; it does NOT need a session to babysit accumulation. Method when surface-ready: (a) grep `git log --grep='cycle 15' --grep='response.usage'` for the per-mechanism observation rows; (b) compute a noise-tolerant percentile per mechanism (working starting point: `max(observed) × 1.5` OR `p95 × 1.2`, whichever is higher — pick after looking at actual variance); (c) land a Red→Green cycle in `test_anthropic_backend_integration.py` adding `_TOKEN_USAGE_CEILING_<MECHANISM>: Final[int] = N` constants and asserting `response.usage.input_tokens + response.usage.output_tokens < _TOKEN_USAGE_CEILING_*` per parametrized branch; (d) commit message records the observation set and the percentile choice. Blast radius: `tests/v3/extraction/test_anthropic_backend_integration.py` only. Does NOT touch `anthropic_backend.py` (no `_last_usage` attribute added per plan-group #14 M4 + I1 resolution). Cross-references: plan-group #14 instrumentation cycle 15 (`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-05-14-anthropic-extraction-backend-instrumentation.md`); auto-memory `project-anthropic-api-credit-cap`; auto-memory `project-anthropic-api-gate-outcomes`. Suggested dispatch tier: code-chore interpretive (sonnet) — selecting the percentile from observed variance is light judgment beyond mechanical transcription.

chore.synopsis: Amend spec §5.3 step 4 to add an explicit dematerialization branch for the (post-mutation no-co_grantor state + already-populated co_grantor) case. Resolves contradiction with §6.7 row 1's jt_mr_to_in_um expected_co_grantor_present=False.

chores.chore:
Current §5.3 step 4 covers only (i) "post-mutation should-exist + currently None → materialize as GrantorInfo()" and (ii) "already populated → preserve". It does NOT cover (iii) "post-mutation should-NOT-exist + already populated", which is the case §6.7 row 1 (jt_mr_to_in_um) lands in. Seed (JT, MR) `promote_seed`s to a TrustData with co_grantor = GrantorInfo() (materialized-but-empty per `promote_seed` spec §6.2.3). Parser then transitions to (IN, UM). §5.3 step 4 as written says preserve; §6.7 row 1 expects co_grantor absent. Lead resolution (option a, approved 2026-05-18): add a conditional dematerialization branch distinguishing seed-materialized-empty from paralegal-populated.
Amendment to §5.3 step 4 (lead-approved verbatim text — insert as a new bullet between the existing "materialization" rule and the "preservation" rule):
> **Dematerialization branch:** if the post-mutation state is one where `co_grantor` should NOT exist (`trust_type != JOINT` AND `marital_status != MARRIED`) AND `result.co_grantor` is a default-only `GrantorInfo()` (no fields populated beyond schema defaults — check via `result.co_grantor == GrantorInfo()`), dematerialize by setting `result.co_grantor = None`. If `result.co_grantor` is populated (any field differs from schema defaults), preserve it; the populated data is meaningful and dropping it would breach the bounded-context translation invariant.
The existing "If `co_grantor` is already populated, preserve it ..." sentence remains as the fallback when the dematerialization branch does not fire.
Also: add a new Decision log entry (Decision #21): "Distinguish seed-materialized-empty from paralegal-populated co_grantor in §5.3 step 4. Dematerialize the former on post-mutation no-co_grantor states; preserve the latter unconditionally. Resolves contradiction with §6.7 row 1 (jt_mr_to_in_um)."
Blast radius: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-23-parser-migration-design.md` only. No `src/` or `tests/` change. No `splits.xml` or `plans.xml` change.
Method: mechanical edit at fixed location. Insert the new bullet text between line 207 (the existing "If `co_grantor` is already populated" sentence) and the next protocol bullet (about "Combinatorial cycle-5 coverage"); append a Decision #21 entry at the end of the Decision log table near line 892.
Suggested dispatch tier: simple-chore mechanical (gpt-5-mini) — purely text edit at explicit locations with lead-provided verbatim replacement text.
Cross-references: plan-group #15 plan-md `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-04-23-parser-migration-docx.md` (cycle §6.7 implementation depends on this amendment landing; the plan-md will cite chore #37 as the authority for the dematerialization branch); spec sections §5.3 step 4 (line 207), §6.7 row 1 (line 578), Decision log (line 892).

chore.synopsis: Codify splits.xml convention: in pixi-managed projects, when a plan-group's blast-radius includes pyproject.toml, it implicitly includes pixi.toml + pixi.lock as transactional mirrors of the same logical pin.

chores.chore:
Surfaced during exec-multi-plan for plan-group 2026-05-14-anthropic-extraction-backend wave 1 cycle 4 (commit ff50cf7): `pixi add --pypi anthropic` is a transactional operation that atomically edits pyproject.toml, pixi.toml, and pixi.lock. The cycle's splits.xml blast-radius declared pyproject.toml only, leaving pixi.toml + pixi.lock outside scope; splitting them would force pixi.lock drift (the resolved env state would no longer match the declared pin), a strictly worse failure mode than mild blast-radius widening.
The lead-user policy decision (recorded 2026-05-19): accept cycle 4 as-is, codify the rule for future plan-groups via this chore.
Remediation scope (simple chore, doc-only):
1. CLAUDE.md (`/home/ramda/code/trust-generator/CLAUDE.md`) — add a sentence to the "Conventions" section stating: "In any plan-group whose blast-radius includes `pyproject.toml`, the blast-radius implicitly extends to `pixi.toml` and `pixi.lock` for the duration of dep-add cycles (atomic-edit semantics of `pixi add --pypi`). Plans should NOT enumerate pixi.toml/pixi.lock separately in splits.xml; treat them as transactional mirrors of the pyproject pin."
2. (Optional, non-blocking) `.claude/context/schema/splits.xsd` — consider whether to encode this rule schematically (likely not — schema is structural, this rule is semantic). If not encoded, the CLAUDE.md statement is canonical.
Blast radius: `CLAUDE.md` only. No `src/` or `tests/` change. No `splits.xml` or `plans.xml` change. No `pixi.toml`/`pixi.lock` change (this chore documents the rule that just got exercised; the dep-add itself is already committed).
Method: mechanical text-insertion at a documented location. Suggested dispatch tier: simple-chore mechanical (gpt-5-mini) or simple-chore interpretive (gpt-5.4-mini) if the wording requires tuning for project tone.
Cross-references: plan-group #14 wave-1 cycle 4 commit ff50cf7 (the precipitating deviation); CLAUDE.md "Conventions" section (target of the edit).

chore.synopsis: Fix the test-model-coupling invariant in the anthropic-extraction-backend sequence.xml: it checks a non-existent `AnthropicBackend.__init__` `model` default (spec §6 forbids it). Re-author the gate to check _TEST_MODEL == _DEFAULT_MODEL coherence.

chores.chore:
During the wave-2 gate execution of plan-group 2026-05-14-anthropic-extraction-backend, the `test-model-coupling` invariant's `peer-symbol-check` gate failed. The gate command is:
`pixi run python -c "import inspect; from trust_generator.v3.extraction.anthropic_backend import AnthropicBackend; from tests.v3.extraction.test_anthropic_backend import _TEST_MODEL; sig = inspect.signature(AnthropicBackend.__init__); default = sig.parameters['model'].default; assert default == _TEST_MODEL, ...; print('ok')"`
The gate presupposes `AnthropicBackend.__init__` has a *default* value for the `model` parameter. It does not — and cannot: spec §6 (design-md line 634) explicitly states "The constructor takes `model` as a required argument. The spec does not commit to a default ... Hard-coding a default in code is rejected — `model` stays required to keep the `backend_id` honest." So `sig.parameters['model'].default` is `inspect._empty`, and the gate's `assert default == _TEST_MODEL` fails by construction.
The invariant was authored (during sequence-multi-plan) against a counterfactual spec where the ctor carries a default. The implementation correctly followed the actual spec.
DISPOSITION TAKEN (lead-user decision, 2026-05-19): the invariant's *intent* — prevent silent drift between the test model and the production/canonical model — is preserved by the implementation. A substitute check was run inline during the wave-2 gate and PASSED:
`pixi run python -c "from tests.v3.extraction.test_anthropic_backend import _TEST_MODEL; from tests.v3.extraction.test_anthropic_backend_integration import _DEFAULT_MODEL; assert _TEST_MODEL == _DEFAULT_MODEL; print('ok')"`
Both constants equal "claude-sonnet-4-6". The plan-group was closed on the substitute check; this chore tracks the sequence.xml correction.
Remediation scope (simple chore, mechanical):
Edit `docs/superpowers/multi/2026-05-14-anthropic-extraction-backend-sequence.xml`, the `test-model-coupling` invariant block (around lines 86-91): - Replace the `peer-symbol-check` gate command with the substitute form: assert `tests.v3.extraction.test_anthropic_backend._TEST_MODEL == tests.v3.extraction.test_anthropic_backend_integration._DEFAULT_MODEL`. - Update the `<constraint>` text to describe the actual drift surface (two test-file model constants must agree), not a non-existent ctor default.
IMPORTANT: land AFTER plan-group 2026-05-14-anthropic-extraction-backend closes (sequence.xml read-only during execution per spec-pipeline invariant #13). By the time this chore is dispatched the plan-group is already closed, so the read-only constraint no longer binds.
Blast radius: `docs/superpowers/multi/2026-05-14-anthropic-extraction-backend-sequence.xml` only.
Method: mechanical edit at a fixed invariant block. Suggested dispatch tier: simple-chore interpretive (gpt-5.4-mini) — the constraint-text rewrite needs light interpretation.

chore.synopsis: spec-pipeline chore-authoring (ingest-spec, scope-maintenance) wrote chores #38-41 violating chores.xsd — over-length attrs, missing baseline, unescaped tag — no validation gate. Add an XSD-validation step to chore authoring; audit for drift.

chores.chore:
During the session closing chores #38-41 (2026-05-21), `chores.xml` was found to fail `chores.xsd` validation, and had been failing since those entries were authored on 2026-05-19 (commits 8fd8aee / f072ee0 / ea01891). Four violation classes: `origin` over the 60-char `_short_desc` limit on all four; `synopsis` over the 250-char `_long_desc` limit on #41; the required `baseline` attribute missing on all four; an unescaped `<constraint>` tag in #41's body making the file non-well-formed XML. The entries themselves were repaired in commit 99da9a9.
Root cause (what this chore tracks): the spec-pipeline chore-authoring workflows — `ingest-spec` and the `scope-maintenance` protocol that plan/chore executors use to raise mid-execution chore-entries — write `<chore>` elements with no XSD-validation step. Two days of malformed canonical state went uncaught.
Remediation (lands in the spec-pipeline plugin SOURCE repo, crosbycrosbylaw-plugins-official — NOT this repo, and NOT the plugin cache, which is overwritten on plugin update): 1. Add an XSD-validation step (`xmllint --noout --schema` or equivalent) to every workflow that writes `chores.xml` or `plans.xml` — `ingest-spec`, `scope-maintenance`, and the status-flip step of `exec-code-chore` / `exec-simple-chore` — blocking on validation failure. 2. Consider a pre-commit gate or PostToolUse hook as a defense-in-depth backstop. 3. Audit the current `chores.xml` and `plans.xml` for any other latent violations.
Blast radius: spec-pipeline plugin source files only (workflow reference XMLs, SKILL.md, scripts). No trust-generator `src/`, `tests/`, or repo-file change. Tracked in this registry because that is where the symptom surfaced; the fix is cross-project.
Dispatch: NOT suitable for routine `exec-simple-chore` (copilot-cli) dispatch — the remediation is cross-project design work (gate placement, failure surfacing). Handle as a dedicated session in the plugin source repo.
Cross-references: chores #38-41 (the malformed entries); repair commit 99da9a9; `chores.xsd` `_short_desc` / `_long_desc` / `_hash` facets; chore #34 (sibling spec-pipeline convention-drift tracking — consider batching).

chore.synopsis: coercion.py robustness: _to_address must preserve the Address.country='US' schema default on 3-part input and warn on 4+ comma parts; _to_person_reference must narrow its except ValidationError and log a warning.

chores.chore:
Three coercion.py findings from the 2026-05-21 pr-review-toolkit pass (code-reviewer + silent-failure-hunter).
1. H1 — `_to_address` (coercion.py ~line 106) passes `country=""` to `Address()` for 3-part input, clobbering the schema default `country="US"` (schema.py:273). Fix: omit the `country` kwarg unless a 4th part is present. The 3-part test (test_coercion.py) must gain a `country == "US"` assertion. 2.
